title: The aggregation pipeline, and where it beats a loop in the application

videos.script: The finance team wants revenue per month. You could fetch every order and add them up in your program. {{loop}} Or you could send the server a list of steps and let it do the adding. That list is the aggregation pipeline. {{pipeline}} Each stage takes documents in and passes documents on. Match keeps some, group adds them up, sort puts them in order, project shapes what comes out. {{stages}} Then the order lines. Unwind turns one order with three lines into three documents. Lookup fetches the product's name from another collection. Together they give you the best sellers. {{unwind}} Then the race. The same total, once by a loop that pulls a hundred thousand orders across the connection, and once by the pipeline. {{race}} The loop moves twenty-four megabytes and takes seconds. The pipeline sends back one document. And the loop gets the money wrong, because it added in doubles. {{money}} Last, what the pipeline needs from you: a match first, so it can use an index, and an eye on memory, because a stage that sorts has a limit. {{limits}}
